critiques.summary: H1 is well supported and correctly ranked first. The causal chain is now grounded in verified findings at every hop that matters: an expired client certificate (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) presented by payment-service (F30/F35) is rejected at the TLS handshake from 12:15:27Z (F7/F20/F27), producing exactly 100% bank_api_error_rate and a ~97-point payment_success_rate collapse first deviating in the 12:15 bucket with a verified flat pre-onset baseline back to 10:00Z (F8/F9/F25/F26/F29), while failures are logged as PENDING_RETRY and never bump the 5xx error_rate panel (F10/F12) and latency DROPs, consistent with fast handshake rejection rather than timeouts (F11). The failure mode is unambiguous: F27/F28 show 0 timeout and 0 5xx signatures, so the 100% bank error is TLS-handshake rejection, not a partner 5xx or an induced timeout. Alternatives genuinely fail on mechanism or scope: H2 is contradicted by the client-side 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client...' log and the latency drop; H3 has no mechanism and the 11:20 gap is shown real in 60s buckets; H4/H5 are contradicted by F13-F17 (ledger-db, db_pool, api-gateway healthy and silent at onset). Two premises remain genuinely unverifiable rather than untested — (a) whether CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal is our own credential or partner-issued (no cert/secret store exists; T4 exhausted both tool paths), and (b) the ~40 support tickets' content (no ticket/CRM telemetry exists, F19) — but neither can change the ranking, since H2 would require an alert-45 signature that is mechanically a client-cert expiry, and H1's defect and outcome are identical under either ownership reading. The only obtainable-but-untested path is kafka consumer-lag (H4's co-tenant route), which cannot produce an exact 100% 'expired certificate' alert even if congested. No blocking issue remains; the confidence cap reflects the unattributed certificate and the inferred customer-impact link, and the root-cause statement should not claim credential ownership.

This does not change which hypothesis is top or the observed mechanism/outcome, but the root-cause statement must not claim 'payment-service-owned credential' as verified.

The customer-impact hop (~40 support tickets map to this exact bank-call failure) is ASSUMED, not verified: no ticket/CRM telemetry exists (F19). The link rests on matching rate (~1.4/min) and timing (12:17Z ticket onset vs 12:15:27Z failures), which is plausible but not confirmed. A coincident distinct client-app issue cannot be formally excluded from telemetry, though no client-app error signature exists (F23).

Kafka consumer-lag / settlement-service queue backlog was never enumerated (no consumer-lag metric obtained, queue hop unverified). This is the only obtainable-but-untested path to a co-tenant cause, but it cannot produce the observed exact 100% 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' signature (F27/F28), so it cannot displace H1.

H2 rests partly on absence of evidence within payment-service logs (0 '5xx' matches) rather than positive partner-side telemetry, and bank-partner-api has no observability (F3/F18). But the positive client-side alert-45 log and the fast-fail latency drop are affirmative evidence against a partner-side 5xx/degradation, so H2 is contradicted, not merely unsupported.
